front.title: Protected Transaction Authority and Execution-Finality Boundaries for Delegated Digital Operations

abstract.t: Recent publicly reported incidents involving unauthorized use of legitimately signed account-delegation and asset-transfer operations have exposed a gap between cryptographic validity and permission to perform an exact consequential act. This document proposes an experimental, transport-independent execution-finality protocol for delegated digital operations. A Candidate Act is placed in a non- effective state; protected collection-time and execution-time enforcement domains bind approved intent, independently reconstruct the pending effect, and require an unforgeable, sink-specific, single-use authorization before signing, dispatching, transmitting, exporting, or actuating. The protocol specifies state continuity, revocation, nonce burn, quota settlement, delegated-code controls, multi-domain interoperability, failure behavior, receipts, conformance tests, and migration profiles. It includes ASCII sequence diagrams and flowcharts, complete executable Python, Go, and JavaScript reference listings, a reproducible test-vector generator and runner, and recorded cross-language test results in informative appendices. This is a proposal for discussion, not an adopted IETF standard; the reference code is not production cryptographic custody software.
